headline: 11-party alliance claims public trust in govt has hit rock bottom
summary: The Jamaat-led alliance cites mismanagement, energy crises, and foreign policy failures as reasons for the decline in public confidence.
details: The Jamaat-led 11-party alliance stated on Sunday that public trust in the government has reached its lowest point over the last six months.
Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizen Party and opposition chief whip, shared this assessment following a meeting at the leader of the opposition's residence in Dhaka.
The alliance pointed to failures in implementing the public mandate of the referendum and the refusal to take oath for the Constitution Reform Council as primary causes.
Nahid Islam criticized the government's 180 days of tenure, describing it as rife with mismanagement, including record-high load-shedding and fuel and gas shortages.
The alliance highlighted that hundreds of factories are shutting down and farmers are facing a fertilizer crisis, while the government allegedly paints a picture of success.
The opposition also criticized the cabinet reshuffle, claiming it shows a lack of proper planning and that more reshuffles will be necessary as ministers fail.
Regarding foreign policy, the alliance expressed concern over the government's failure to hold India accountable for allowing Awami League activities in Delhi.
The 11-party alliance has scheduled a series of 'long marches' starting September 5 from Dhaka to Chattogram, with subsequent marches to Rangpur, Jashore, and Sylhet.
The alliance believes Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to India will not benefit the country until justice for Sheikh Hasina and the killers of Osman Hadi is ensured.
caption:
Public trust in the government has hit 'rock bottom' according to the 11-party alliance.

The Jamaat-led 11-party alliance stated on Sunday that public trust in the government has reached its lowest point over the last six months.

Nahid Islam, convener of the National Citizen Party and opposition chief whip, shared this assessment following a meeting at the leader of the opposition's residence in Dhaka.

The alliance pointed to failures in implementing the public mandate of the referendum and the refusal to take oath for the Constitution Reform Council as primary causes.

Nahid Islam criticized the government's 180 days of tenure, describing it as rife with mismanagement, including record-high load-shedding and fuel and gas shortages.

The alliance highlighted that hundreds of factories are shutting down and farmers are facing a fertilizer crisis, while the government allegedly paints a picture of success.

The opposition also criticized the cabinet reshuffle, claiming it shows a lack of proper planning and that more reshuffles will be necessary as ministers fail.

Regarding foreign policy, the alliance expressed concern over the government's failure to hold India accountable for allowing Awami League activities in Delhi.

The 11-party alliance has scheduled a series of 'long marches' starting September 5 from Dhaka to Chattogram, with subsequent marches to Rangpur, Jashore, and Sylhet.

The alliance believes Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's visit to India will not benefit the country until justice for Sheikh Hasina and the killers of Osman Hadi is ensured.

headline: Police fired tear gas and pellets into a mosque during July prayers
summary: A madrasa teacher's testimony at the International Crimes Tribunal details violent police actions during the July uprising, including attacks on worshippers and students.
details: A teacher at Jatrabari Jamia Islamia Darul Ulum Madrasa testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-2 on Sunday, stating that police fired tear gas, sound grenades, and pellets into a mosque during Friday prayers on July 19, 2024.

The witness, Muhammad Ridwan Hassan, stated that in protest of the mosque attack, students and worshippers took to the streets, resulting in the deaths of 23 to 24 madrasa students across the country that day.
Hassan's testimony also detailed the death of 14-year-old Ahmad Abdullah on July 18, who was allegedly shot and then crushed by a police armored vehicle.
He further testified that on July 20, police shot and killed Imam Hassan (Taim), the son of a police officer, near the Kazla flyover during a period when the curfew was relaxed.
On August 3, Hassan described seeing armed Chhatra League and Jubo League members positioned near the Shonir Akhra bridge, acting aggressively with the support of police.

He also recounted the events of August 5, claiming that police and BGB killed approximately 60 people, including 5 to 6 madrasa students and scholars, in Jatrabari as protesters marched toward Ganabhaban.
The witness called for the justice and trial of those involved in the killings, including members of the Awami League, its affiliate organizations, and law enforcement agencies.
The case involves 11 accused, nine of whom are currently fugitives, including former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman and several other high-ranking police officials.
caption:
Police fired tear gas and pellets into a mosque during Friday prayers in July, a witness testified.

A teacher at Jatrabari Jamia Islamia Darul Ulum Madrasa testified at the International Crimes Tribunal-2 on Sunday, stating that police fired tear gas, sound grenades, and pellets into a mosque during Friday prayers on July 19, 2024.

The witness, Muhammad Ridwan Hassan, stated that in protest of the mosque attack, students and worshippers took to the streets, resulting in the deaths of 23 to 24 madrasa students across the country that day.

Hassan's testimony also detailed the death of 14-year-old Ahmad Abdullah on July 18, who was allegedly shot and then crushed by a police armored vehicle.

He further testified that on July 20, police shot and killed Imam Hassan (Taim), the son of a police officer, near the Kazla flyover during a period when the curfew was relaxed.

On August 3, Hassan described seeing armed Chhatra League and Jubo League members positioned near the Shonir Akhra bridge, acting aggressively with the support of police.

He also recounted the events of August 5, claiming that police and BGB killed approximately 60 people, including 5 to 6 madrasa students and scholars, in Jatrabari as protesters marched toward Ganabhaban.

The witness called for the justice and trial of those involved in the killings, including members of the Awami League, its affiliate organizations, and law enforcement agencies.

The case involves 11 accused, nine of whom are currently fugitives, including former DMP Commissioner Habibur Rahman and several other high-ranking police officials.
